label: Scoped certificate-calibrated correction procedure
definition: A procedure supplies a Boolean decision, a natural-number certificate, a Boolean checker and an execution-resource predicate on evidence. Covered requires availability and accepted output certificates at every scoped state. Calibrated requires every accepted answer at a scoped state to agree in both directions with the supplied correctness predicate. These are separate conditional assumptions on arbitrary domains, not a complete warrant theory.
note: Analyst candidate with attribution deferred. A checker accepting its own answer can be wrong; identity evidence need not come with execution resources. Availability is an explicit open resource relation, not adequate epistemic justification. Calibration is a semantic assumption; its epistemic accessibility and applicability to actual inquiry remain open. The example is a toy certificate protocol, not a reconstruction of the original warranted correction sense.
